stanzas: أمِنْ تذَكُّرِ جيرانٍ بذي سلمِ
مزجتَ دمعاً جرى من مقلةٍ بدمِ
أمْ هبَّتِ الريحُ من تلقاءِ كاظمةٍ
وأوْمَضَ البَرْقُ في الظلْماءِ مِنْ إضَمِ
فما لعينيكَ إن قلتَ اكففا هَمَتا
ومَا لِقَلْبِك إنْ قُلْتَ اسْتَفِقْ يَهِمِ
أَيَحْسَبُ الصَّبُّ أنَّ الحُبَّ مُنْكتِمٌ
ما بَيْنَ مُنْسَجِم منهُ ومضطَرِمِ
لولاَ الهَوَى لَمْ تُرِقْ دَمْعاً عَلَى طَلَلٍ
ولا أرقتَ لذكرِ البانِ والعَلمِ
فكيفَ تُنْكِرُ حُبَّا بعدَ ما شَهِدَتْ
بهِ عليكَ عدولُ الدَّمْعِ والسَّقَم
وَأثْبَتَ الوجْدُ خَطَّيْ عَبْرَةٍ وضَنًى
مِثْلَ البَهارِ عَلَى خَدَّيْكَ والعَنَمِ
نعمْ سرى طيفُ من أهوى فأرقني
والحُبُّ يَعْتَرِضُ اللَّذاتِ بالأَلَمِ
يا لائِمِي في الهَوَى العُذْرِيِّ مَعْذِرَةً
منِّي إليكَ ولو أنصفتَ لم تلُمِ
عَدَتْكَ حالِيَ لا سِرِّي بمُسْتَتِرٍ
عن الوُشاةِ ولادائي بمنحسمِ
مَحَّضَتْنِي النُّصْحَ لكِنْ لَسْتُ أَسْمَعُهُ
إنَّ المُحِبَّ عَن العُذَّالِ في صَمَمِ
إني اتهمتُ نصيحَ الشيبِ في عذلٍ
والشَّيْبُ أَبْعَدُ في نُصْحٍ عَنِ التُّهَم
orig.credit: al-Busiri, Qasidat al-Burda (13th century): the first chapter, on love-longing

stanzas: Is it from remembering neighbours at Dhū Salam
that you have mixed tears flowing from your eye with blood?
Or has the wind blown from the direction of Kāẓima,
and lightning flashed in the darkness from Iḍam?
What ails your eyes, that when you say "hold back" they stream,
and your heart, that when you say "come to your senses" it wanders?
Does the lover think that love can be hidden,
between a flood of tears and a heart on fire?
Were it not for passion you would not shed tears over a ruin,
nor lie sleepless at the mention of the willow and the mountain.
So how can you deny a love,
when the honest witnesses of tears and sickness have testified against you?
Longing has fixed two lines of weeping and wasting
on your cheeks, like the yellow of narcissus and the red of the ʿanam berry.
Yes, the phantom of the one I love came by night and kept me awake;
love blocks pleasure with pain.
You who blame me for a chaste love, accept my excuse;
had you been fair, you would not blame.
May my state pass you by: my secret is not hidden
from slanderers, nor is my sickness cut off.
You gave me sincere advice, but I do not hear it;
the lover is deaf to those who reproach.
I even suspected the counsel of grey hair in its reproach,
though grey hair is the furthest of advisers from suspicion.
A-min tadhakkuri jīrānin bi-Dhī Salami
mazajta damʿan jarā min muqlatin bi-dami
Am habbati r-rīḥu min tilqāʾi Kāẓimatin
wa-awmaḍa l-barqu fi ẓ-ẓalmāʾi min Iḍami
Fa-mā li-ʿaynayka in qulta kfufā hamatā
wa-mā li-qalbika in qulta stafiq yahimi
A-yaḥsabu ṣ-ṣabbu anna l-ḥubba munkatimun
mā bayna munsajimin minhu wa-muḍṭarimi
Lawlā l-hawā lam turiq damʿan ʿalā ṭalalin
wa-lā ariqta li-dhikri l-bāni wa-l-ʿalami
Fa-kayfa tunkiru ḥubban baʿda mā shahidat
bihi ʿalayka ʿudūlu d-damʿi wa-s-saqami
Wa-athbata l-wajdu khaṭṭay ʿabratin wa-ḍanan
mithla l-bahāri ʿalā khaddayka wa-l-ʿanami
Naʿam sarā ṭayfu man ahwā fa-arraqanī
wa-l-ḥubbu yaʿtariḍu l-ladhdhāti bi-l-alami
Yā lāʾimī fi l-hawā l-ʿudhriyyi maʿdhiratan
minnī ilayka wa-law anṣafta lam talumi
ʿAdatka ḥāliya lā sirrī bi-mustatirin
ʿani l-wushāti wa-lā dāʾī bi-munḥasimi
Maḥḥaḍatniya n-nuṣḥa lākin lastu asmaʿuhu
inna l-muḥibba ʿani l-ʿudhdhāli fī ṣamami
Innī ttahamtu naṣīḥa sh-shaybi fī ʿadhalin
wa-sh-shaybu abʿadu fī nuṣḥin ʿani t-tuhami

notes: The text is the poem's first chapter, the nasīb or love-prelude, one verse to a stanza: twelve of its about 160 verses. The refrain sung between verses in many performances ("Mawlāya ṣalli wa-sallim …") is a later addition and is not part of this edition.
Verses 1–2: Dhū Salam, Kāẓima and Iḍam are places on the way to Medina, which is how the love-prelude turns, in the second chapter, into praise of the Prophet.
Verse 5: the willow (bān) and the mountain (ʿalam) are stock images of the beloved's camp in Arabic love poetry.
Verse 7: the ʿanam is a shrub with red fruit or blossom; with the yellow narcissus (bahār) it pictures cheeks yellowed by wasting and reddened by bloody tears.
